title: ArcherSTEM
subtitle: Educational publishing & interactive STEM learning ecosystem

plain.problem: Delivering modern STEM, coding, and financial literacy curricula across print workbooks and instant digital downloads is complex for educational publishers.
plain.built: Architected and deployed ArcherSTEM on WordPress with a custom digital eBook portal, fillable PDF downloads, curriculum alignment standards, and automated checkout.
plain.outcome: A high-retention educational publishing platform serving students, adult learners, and school districts with instant digital asset access.

engineer.problem: Managing heavy digital PDF distribution, student workbook licensing, standards-compliant taxonomy (Jump$tart & CEE benchmarks), and secure payment processing on a content-heavy CMS.
how: Configured WordPress infrastructure with WooCommerce digital licensing and automated watermarked PDF fulfillment.
Engineered a responsive student workbook resource portal with interactive exercise downloads and QR-linked companion solutions.
Implemented structured schema markup (EducationalWork & Product) for optimal search discovery across educational institutions.
Configured server-side caching (LiteSpeed) and WebP image optimization to maintain sub-second page loads.
tradeoffs: Custom WordPress CMS over headless LMS
Far faster authoring workflow for curriculum writers, in exchange for monolithic backend coupling
Server-side caching over dynamic client rendering
Significantly reduced server TTFB for search visitors, requiring cache purging on book updates

diagram.ariaLabel: ArcherSTEM architecture: student visitor, WordPress LMS engine, WooCommerce digital checkout, secure download vault, and curriculum delivery portal.

title: ScienceQuick
subtitle: Evidence-based health, nutrition & holistic science publication

plain.problem: Complex medical and biological research (metabolism, cellular aging, nutrition) is often locked behind academic jargon and sluggish, ad-bloated media sites.
plain.built: Built and deployed ScienceQuick as a lightning-fast digital publication on WordPress that translates clinical research into accessible, evidence-backed guides.
plain.outcome: A clean, high-performance science magazine delivering actionable health knowledge with instant page loads.

engineer.problem: Maximizing organic search ranking and mobile reader retention for scientific journalism requiring fast typography rendering, extensive categorization, and high Core Web Vitals scores.
how: Engineered a minimalist, typography-first WordPress theme optimized for mobile readability and zero layout shifts (CLS < 0.01).
Configured Redis object caching and edge CDN caching on Cloudflare for 98% static asset hit ratio.
Implemented MedicalWebPage and Article JSON-LD schema for Google scientific search snippets.
Automated WebP media conversion pipelines reducing payload weight by 68%.
tradeoffs: Static edge caching over dynamic recommendation widgets
Maximized mobile load speeds at the expense of individualized content personalization
Lightweight custom theme over multi-purpose page builders
Cleaner DOM tree and higher PageSpeed scores, requiring code updates for layout revisions

diagram.ariaLabel: ScienceQuick architecture: mobile reader, Cloudflare Edge CDN, Redis Object Cache, WordPress publishing engine, and SEO structured output.

title: Annals of Curiosity
subtitle: Scholarly peer-reviewed medical journals & research education platform

plain.problem: Medical and epidemiological research teams need an official publishing platform for peer-reviewed studies and clinical courses without prohibitive institutional journal fees.
plain.built: Architected a dedicated academic journal platform on WordPress hosting two peer-reviewed publications, clinical research training modules, and an open scientific monograph repository.
plain.outcome: An open-access scholarly publishing hub empowering medical researchers and clinicians to publish and learn.

engineer.problem: Supporting strict scholarly publishing protocols (peer review lifecycle, issue/volume archiving, citation metadata, and editorial workflows) without expensive proprietary journal software.
how: Constructed custom post types and taxonomies for journal volumes, issues, authors, and citation indices across ACE and ACSC journals.
Implemented Dublin Core and Google Scholar meta tag generators for direct academic indexing.
Integrated a structured research methodology course portal with student enrollment and material downloads.
Hardened WordPress security headers and configured automated database backups for research data integrity.
tradeoffs: WordPress custom taxonomy over Open Journal Systems (OJS)
Unmatched UI design freedom and mobile accessibility, requiring custom bibliographic metadata formatting
Open-access repository over paywalled access
Direct global clinician impact, traded for institutional subscription revenue models

diagram.ariaLabel: Annals of Curiosity architecture: researchers and authors, editorial desk, custom taxonomy engine, peer-review archive, and academic search indexing.

title: Automated FIFA Commentary Engine
subtitle: Real-time AI football commentary with Computer Vision, NLP & TTS

plain.problem: Generating live, engaging play-by-play commentary for match footage currently requires human commentators, making amateur, simulated, or replay games silent or repetitive.
plain.built: An end-to-end AI pipeline that watches football match video, tracks players and the ball, classifies 13 match events, and generates professional broadcast audio commentary with synchronized speech.
plain.outcome: Broadcast-quality play-by-play commentary synthesized and synced directly into match video automatically.

engineer.problem: Extracting match context from dense video, tracking multiple players and the ball simultaneously, and producing coherent commentary with human broadcaster pacing and tone.
how: Frame-by-frame analysis using YOLOv8 for player (person) and ball (sports_ball) localization.
ByteTrack-based multi-object tracking to assign persistent IDs across frames with occlusion handling.
GPT-4o-mini Vision classifies 13 match events (goals, passes, tackles, fouls, shots, celebrations) with confidence scoring.
Event aggregation handles batching, cooldowns (7s on goals), and noise suppression.
GPT commentary engine uses a specialized sports broadcast prompt pacing narration at ~2.2 words/second.
OpenAI TTS-1 synthesizes lifelike speech audio, composited into the final video via MoviePy.
tradeoffs: Sampling every 90th frame over continuous inference
Dramatically reduced compute cost and latency with negligible loss in event detection
ByteTrack over deep appearance re-ID
Faster real-time tracking performance on CPU/modest GPU without heavyweight feature extraction

diagram.ariaLabel: FIFA Commentary Pipeline: video input, YOLOv8 detection, ByteTrack tracking, GPT-4o Vision event classifier, GPT commentary generator, OpenAI TTS, and final video compositor.

title: 3D Scanner & Image-to-3D Generator
subtitle: Open-source local image-to-3D pipeline with hardware turntable integration

plain.problem: Creating textured 3D digital models from physical items normally requires expensive photogrammetry rigs or costly cloud subscriptions with recurring usage fees.
plain.built: Developed a 100% local, open-source 3D generation system that takes images and outputs Blender-ready studio models in seconds with Arduino turntable hardware support.
plain.outcome: Drop an image, get fully textured 3D models (GLB, OBJ, STL, FBX, .blend) locally on your own machine with zero cloud costs.

engineer.problem: Delivering fast, high-fidelity single-image 3D mesh reconstruction locally on consumer GPUs while automating hardware turntable scanning.
how: Integrates TripoSR neural reconstruction model locally (runs on 4GB+ VRAM or CPU fallback).
Builds a PyQt6 desktop control interface interfacing with Arduino stepper motors for 360-degree turntable capture.
Automates multi-format mesh export: GLB, OBJ, STL (3D printing), FBX, and native .blend files.
Generates studio-lit Blender scenes with automated camera positioning, lighting, and PBR material setup.
tradeoffs: Local TripoSR over cloud APIs
Zero operating costs and total privacy, requiring minimum 4GB local GPU for 5-second inference
Arduino serial control over custom hardware PCB
Accessible to any maker and hobbyist with off-the-shelf components

diagram.ariaLabel: 3D Scanner pipeline: camera and Arduino turntable, image intake, TripoSR neural reconstruction, mesh processing, and multi-format Blender export.

plain.problem: When software changes, the instructions that describe it quietly go out of date, and customers and new hires get confused.
plain.built: DocSentry watches every code change, finds the documentation affected, and either reports the mismatch or proposes the fix automatically.
plain.outcome: Documentation that stays correct without someone checking it by hand.

engineer.problem: Code changes faster than the docs that describe it. Reviewers don't catch the drift, and stale docs become support tickets. DocSentry reads each change as structure, finds the docs it affects, and either files a verified issue or proposes the fix.
how: Parses git diffs into Tree-sitter ASTs so changes are reasoned about as functions, signatures and exports, not raw text lines.
Retrieves candidate documentation with hybrid search: BM25 for exact identifiers and flags, dense embeddings (ChromaDB) for paraphrased descriptions.
Validates doc-vs-code consistency with a multi-model evaluator across Groq, Gemini and a local Ollama model.
Opens a GitHub issue or a self-healing fix PR only after the finding has been self-verified.
Ships an interactive static/React monitoring dashboard for runs, findings and outcomes.
tradeoffs: AST-level diffing over line diffs
Needs a grammar per language; unsupported languages fall back to coarse chunks
Hybrid retrieval over embeddings alone
A second index to maintain and a score-fusion step to tune
Multiple model providers with a local fallback
More orchestration code; verdicts need an agreement policy
Self-verification before opening issues
Extra model calls per finding, traded for fewer false-positive issues

diagram.ariaLabel: DocSentry pipeline: git diff to AST parse, hybrid retrieval, multi-model evaluation, self-verification, then GitHub issue or fix PR and a dashboard.

title: Radiology & Document Pipeline
subtitle: Multi-Agent report analyzer with consensus gate and human fallback

plain.problem: One AI reading a medical document can be confidently wrong, and in healthcare that is not acceptable.
plain.built: Several AI reviewers read the same document independently after private details are removed. If they disagree, a human checks it instead of the system guessing.
plain.outcome: Faster document handling with a person always in the loop when it is uncertain.

engineer.problem: A single LLM reading a clinical document can state something false with full confidence. In this setting, a wrong answer is worse than a slow one. The pipeline treats disagreement as a signal and routes it to a person.
how: Multi-agent architecture coordinating parallel specialized critics over medical reports.
Redacts PII/PHI before any text reaches model inference.
Runs parallel specialist critique nodes over the same input to surface unsupported claims.
Computes a consensus score across models; below strict threshold the case is routed to manual triage.
tradeoffs: Redaction before inference
Some context is lost, which can reduce model accuracy on edge cases
Multiple critics in parallel
Higher cost and token usage per document
Strict consensus threshold
More cases land in the human queue; throughput is tuned against safety

diagram.ariaLabel: Radiology pipeline: intake, PII/PHI redaction, three parallel specialist critics, a consensus gate that either releases a structured report or routes to human triage.

title: Real-Time Vehicle & Plate Recognition
subtitle: Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) and tracking

plain.problem: Reading number plates from live video on modest hardware is slow if you process every single frame.
plain.built: The system follows each vehicle through the video and reads its plate once, skipping frames that add nothing, then corrects typical misreads.
plain.outcome: Plate recognition that keeps up with live video on limited hardware.

engineer.problem: Reading plates from a live video stream on constrained hardware means you cannot run every model on every frame. The pipeline spends compute only where it changes the answer.
how: YOLOv8 localizes vehicles and plates on the incoming stream.
SORT / ByteTrack assigns persistent track IDs so each vehicle is read as one entity, not once per frame.
EasyOCR reads the plate crop; custom regex and character-correction post-processing fixes common confusions against expected plate formats.
Frame-skipping heuristics cap per-frame cost for latency-constrained environments.
tradeoffs: Frame skipping
Fast-moving vehicles may be sampled less often; tuned per camera
Tracking before OCR
Added tracker state, in exchange for OCR once per vehicle and consistent IDs
Rule-based correction after OCR
Rules are tied to a plate format and need per-region maintenance
Off-the-shelf OCR
Lower ceiling than a plate-specific trained model, much faster to deploy

diagram.ariaLabel: ANPR pipeline: video stream, frame skipper, YOLOv8 detection, tracker, OCR, character correction and per-track plate output.

plain.problem: Remote access to a Windows computer normally means installing software on every device.
plain.built: PocketDesk streams the desktop straight into a web browser, so nothing needs to be installed on the viewing side.
plain.outcome: Open a link, see the desktop.

engineer.problem: Remote desktop usually means installing a client on the viewing side. PocketDesk streams a Windows desktop to any browser with nothing to install on the viewer's machine.
how: A C# host captures the screen through Win32 GDI.
A Node.js service relays frames over WebSockets.
The browser is the entire client: zero install on the viewing side.
tradeoffs: Win32 GDI capture
Simple and widely compatible, but not the lowest-overhead capture path available on Windows
WebSockets over WebRTC
Simpler to deploy and debug, without WebRTC's adaptive transport
Browser-only client
Limited to what the browser can render and send

diagram.ariaLabel: PocketDesk: a C# Win32 GDI capture host streams to a Node.js WebSocket relay, which serves a browser viewer.
